notes:
Summary of account and technical requirements:
- Business: midsize eDiscovery/compliance vendor supporting law firms and in-house counsel. Primary product is a searchable discovery index for litigation and regulatory investigations.
- Data scale: currently ~120M documents (30TB raw); anticipate growth to 300M+ over 18 months. Indexing cadence: daily ingestion of new corpora + nightly re-index for metadata updates.
- Architecture preference: private deployment (VPC control plane) with on-prem inference nodes inside customer network for PHI/PII workloads. Must support customer-managed KMS/HSM for key custody.
- Search stack: existing inverted-index (Elastic) + separate vector store for semantic search. Want Redwood to handle embedding generation + persistent vector index + reranking pipeline (dense retrieval -> cross-encoder rerank).
- Performance targets: median end-to-end query latency <= 200ms for autocomplete/simple search, <= 600ms for vector+rerank at typical QPS (100–250). P95 requirement for critical workflows <= 1s. Throughput: sustained 250 QPS with bursts to 500 QPS for trials.
- Cost sensitivity: target cost-per-query (avg) < $0.08 for production; willing to pay more for the rerank pass but require cost breakdown (embedding cost, k-NN retrieval, cross-encoder compute). Redwood Optimize recommendations expected to reduce unit cost by batching/caching/prefix reuse.
- Reranking: plan to use a cross-encoder for final ranking on top-50 candidates. Concerned about cross-encoder latency and GPU capacity; evaluating options: distilled cross-encoder vs two-stage rerank with light-weight model + periodic high-fidelity checks.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 + ISO27001 required. Need immutable audit logging (WORM) for 7–10 years, legal-hold capability, and per-request provenance metadata for later subpoena. Data residency: primary US, some EU tenant data for EU clients.
- Retention: document-level retention policies with legal hold overrides. Must support retention locks and export logs for audits.
- Integrations: SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, SIEM syslog for audit streams, support for Splunk/Datadog ingest.
- POC scope (proposed by Redwood): 8-week proof-of-concept covering ingestion pipeline for 5M sample docs, embedding generation, vector index for 50M vectors (approx), rerank prototype on top-50 results, validate latency and cost targets, provide performance tuning playbook.
- Customer quotes: "We cannot accept black-box hosting for client data — need full visibility and auditable controls." — Head of Security.
- Risks: procurement budget cycles (Q2 close), legal still reviewing offsite telemetry, HSM integration is undecided (customer prefers on-prem HSM but asks for Redwood-managed fallback).
- Internal notes: SE to prepare two cost models (GPU-heavy with cheap embeddings vs mixed CPU-embedding + GPU-rerank); include explicit cross-encoder cost per 1k queries. CSM Aisha to prepare onboarding checklist and long-term retention SLA addendum.
- External refs: Drive SOW link above; Fireflies transcript ff_2026-02-12_cb9e2f (security workshop).
- Next immediate action: deliver final POC SOW with network diagram, HSM options, and a sample cost model by 2026-03-05.
